summary: 1. Key operational findings Oct 15 posted 24,304 BCM against a 24,072.2 BCM target (+0.96%), the first daily beat since Oct 12, and MTD narrowed to 436,418 BCM against 469,408.3 (-7.03%), a second straight day of improvement (Oct 13 -7.86%, Oct 14 -7.46%, Oct 15 -7.03%) at day 21 of the 30-day fiscal cycle (9 days remaining). 2. Three things to flag: 1. 3. Material split ran 19.77% Stage 4 / 80.23% Stage 5 -- a partial recovery from Oct 14's 100% Stage 5 day, with EX-340 and EX-247 both moving back into a Stage 4 compartment (730-170), though still short of the "Stage 4 first" priority Ma'aden's Sultan Aljohani confirmed in writing on Oct 15 morning. 2. 4. The crusher logged its fifth straight zero-feed day (0 BCM, the shutdown that began Oct 11); MTD throughput sits at 9,753 LCM against an 86,800 LCM plan (11.24%, down from Oct 14's 11.80%), with no reopening date given. 3. 5. Fleet availability moved in opposite directions on two of the cycle's most-flagged items: EX-263's standing engine-replacement fault (open since 05-Oct, "REPLACING ENGINE") finally cleared at 1:00 PM after 10 days and 230+ breakdown hours, while drilling missed target for the first time since Oct 10 (1,877 m against 2,562.8 m, -26.76%) on 60.5 fleet-wide day-shift standby hours "due to lack of drilling area" plus 16 night-shift hours lost to operator fatigue -- a crew/rostering constraint, not a mechanical one. 6. Fleet availability (Daily Availability Final Report, authoritative over the A&U workbook): excavators 75.60% day / 66.17% MTD, up sharply from Oct 14's 55.95%; trucks 93.39% / 90.57%; drills 85.68% / 86.84%; overall 94.07% / 88.21%, core fleet 91.27%. 7. Lost volume: excavators (EX-253 full day, EX-263 part day before clearing, EX-247 part day) 12,795 BCM / 34,546.5 t at planned rates, down sharply from Oct 14's 15,840-23,040 BCM range; dump trucks (DT-107, DT-109, DT-108) 2,638.4 BCM / 7,123.6 t at today's fleet rate. 8. Combined gross 15,433.4 BCM / 41,670.1 t. 9. EX-247's Oct 14 source conflict (Daily Availability Report: 24 h down at 0.00%; Client Meeting Report: 100% available) does not repeat today -- the two sources now broadly agree (66.67% avail / 8 h down per the Availability Report; 64.58% avail / 56.25% util per the Client Meeting Report, both citing the same engine-warning/low-power fault). Treated as the dispute resolving itself rather than confirmed; flagged below for the site to confirm. Flag, not resolved: a new "ADW-Q4-Recovery Plan" deck/workbook series (v1-Peter-edits through v4_FINAL) appeared in RAW today, named differently from both the existing ADW-Q4-Recovery-and-2027-Budget family tracked in [[q4-recovery-plan-2026]] and the ADW-Q4-DT-Requirement family flagged as a separate, uncompiled document family on 2026-10-16 morning. The naming suggests the site may have merged the two previously separate deck families into one, which would resolve that morning's open merge/split judgment call -- but the files were registered by name only this pass, not read, so this is inferred from filenames and version history, not confirmed content. Worth a dedicated read and compile pass rather than assuming the merge. No new survey file (261016-INX-SUM, carrying the Oct 15 production day's survey reading) had landed by this pass; [[survey-volume-reconciliation]] was not updated and still reflects the Oct 14 reading. The A&U, DPR, Drill Meters, Drill Sampling, Block Info, Equipment Running Hours, Running Hours Maaden, and Distance Report workbooks gained Oct 15 tabs/edits but were registered by name only, not deep-read (the Client Meeting Report and the Daily Availability Final Report cover the figures compiled this pass). Source: KNOWLEDGE/mining_operations_kb/RAW via the librarian compile protocol.
